Primary Care Progress Note
Date: 08/02/2026
Patient: Thomas Goyette, 83-year-old male

Subjective:
Mr. Goyette presents for his routine follow-up. He reports feeling generally well with no new complaints. He denies any recent falls or injuries.

Objective:
Vital signs are stable. Physical examination reveals no acute distress. Cardiovascular, respiratory, and abdominal exams are unremarkable. Musculoskeletal exam shows no tenderness or deformity.

Assessment:
Mr. Goyette is an 83-year-old male with stable health status. No new issues identified at this visit.

Plan:
Continue current management and routine monitoring. Encourage regular physical activity and balanced nutrition. Follow up in 6 months or sooner if any concerns arise.

Radiology Report
Date: 09/20/2026
Patient: Thomas Goyette, 83-year-old male

MRI thoracolumbar spine 09/20/2026: acute osteoporotic L1 compression fracture with bone marrow edema on STIR imaging. Interval increase in L1 vertebral body height loss compared with radiographs from 07/30/2026.

Impression:
There is an acute osteoporotic compression fracture at the L1 vertebral body with bone marrow edema evident on STIR sequences. Interval increase in L1 vertebral body height loss compared with radiographs from 07/30/2026.

notes.author: Interventional radiologist
notes.text:
Spine Intervention Consultation
Date: 09/27/2026
Patient: Thomas Goyette, 83-year-old male

History:
Back pain began 07/27/2026 after bending to pick up a grandchild, 9 weeks before this visit. Pain NRS 6/10 despite 8 weeks of optimal non-surgical management with acetaminophen and calcitonin nasal spray, a thoracolumbar brace and activity modification. Pain has been stable to slightly improved since the fracture.

Clinical Findings:
Back pain localizes to the fractured level; afebrile with no signs of infection or discitis. Seen in the outpatient spine clinic; not hospitalized for this fracture.

Functional Status:
Roland Morris Disability Questionnaire score 19/24.

Management:
Referred for DEXA bone density testing and osteoporosis education; enrolled in the osteoporosis treatment program.

Plan:
Continue current conservative measures and monitor symptoms. Follow up after DEXA testing to discuss further osteoporosis management and potential interventions.
